2: ## ARCH-SAVE-002's fixed 256-byte save header and its 64-byte section descriptors.
3: ##
4: ## WHAT IS IMPLEMENTED, AND WHERE IT IS STATED. Every constant below is transcribed from
5: ## `docs/systems_architecture.md:716-733` -- the save-header offset table and the descriptor
6: ## sentence that follows it. Nothing here is chosen by this module:
7: ##
8: ##   offset 0 magic ASCII `RWLSET01` (8) · 8 format version 1 (u32) · 12 header bytes 256 (u32)
9: ##   16 endian sentinel 16909060 (u32) · 20 section count (u32) · 24 total file bytes (u64)
10: ##   32 completed tick (i64) · 40 rules hash · 72 catalog hash · 104 map hash · 136 integer
11: ##   lookup-table hash · 168 engine patch/build identity hash (32 each) · 200 section table
12: ##   offset, always 256 (u64) · 208 chronicle record count (u64) · 216 replay command sequence
13: ##   at checkpoint (u64) · 224 body digest over table plus section bytes (32).
14: ##
15: ##   Descriptor: `section_id:u32, schema_version:u32, offset:u64, byte_length:u64, row_count:u64,
16: ##   crc32:u32, flags:u32, reserved_zero:24 bytes` = 64 bytes.
17: ##
18: ##   CRC is CRC-32/ISO-HDLC: reversed polynomial 3988292384, initial register 4294967295,
19: ##   reflected bytes, final XOR 4294967295; ASCII `123456789` gives 3421780262. That check vector
20: ##   is asserted in `test_save_header.gd`, so a wrong table cannot pass silently.
21: ##
22: ## THE CATALOG HASH AT OFFSET 72 IS NOT RECOMPUTED HERE. `catalog_ids.gd` already owns that
23: ## digest and names this very offset in its own `SAVE_HEADER_CATALOG_HASH_OFFSET`. This module
24: ## asserts the two constants are equal at load time and delegates the digest to
25: ## `catalog_ids.gd.build()` / `digest_of()`. There is exactly one SHA-256 of the catalog in this
26: ## repository and it is not in this file.
27: ##
28: ## WHAT THIS MODULE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO -- task 09.2 owns all of it and is BLOCKED:
29: ##
30: ##   * BLOCKER H1: the schema version policy. `docs/tasks/09_persistence_replay_reliability.md:17`
31: ##     requires "an explicit version policy before writing release saves" and "do not silently
32: ##     repurpose v1 bytes". So the per-section `schema_version` is carried and range-checked as a
33: ##     u32 and NOTHING here validates its value. The file-level format version IS stated as 1
34: ##     (systems_architecture.md:718) and ARCH-SAVE-005 requires rejecting "future format
35: ##     versions", so that one is checked.
36: ##   * BLOCKER H2: the rules hash (offset 40), map hash (104), integer lookup-table hash (136)
37: ##     and engine build hash (168) have NO producer in this repository. Decision 0034 says so of
38: ##     the rules hash in terms: "the separate offset-40 rules hash, whose serializer does not
39: ##     exist yet either". They are therefore carried as caller-supplied 32-byte digests, checked
40: ##     for length and nothing else. This module does not invent how any of them is computed.
41: ##   * BLOCKER H3: section BODIES. ARCH-SAVE-002 assigns fifteen section IDs and never enumerates
42: ##     their contents; §11 EVENT_SCHEDULE, §13 CHRONICLE and §15 STATE_DIGEST have no owning
43: ##     module at all (`docs/persistence_state_registry.md`, whose section assignment is stated
44: ##     there as its own reading with a basis, not as a quotation). Not one byte of a section body
45: ##     is written or parsed here.
46: ##   * BLOCKER H4: whether section ranges must TILE the file with no gaps. ARCH-SAVE-004 requires
47: ##     "nonoverlapping ranges, exact file length, overflow-safe offsets" and does not say
48: ##     contiguous. `section_table_refusal()` therefore enforces non-overlap, containment and the
49: ##     exact declared file length, and permits a gap. Tightening that is 09.2's call to make.
50: ##
51: ## PERSISTENCE AND DIGEST MEMBERSHIP ARE SEPARATE DIMENSIONS (ARCH-SAVE-007, 2026-09-11). The
52: ## offset-224 body digest and the per-section CRC cover EVERY saved byte, including the host
53: ## debt and six clock counters that ARCH-HASH-001 explicitly excludes from the canonical state
54: ## hash. This module owns the former and not the latter: nothing here computes, stores or
55: ## compares ARCH-HASH-001's `RWL-STATE-1` digest, which belongs to section 15 STATE_DIGEST and
56: ## has no owning module yet. `test_save_header.gd` pins the consequence -- changing a header
57: ## field does not change the body digest, so a changed completed tick is caught by state
58: ## verification rather than by this CRC/SHA pair, exactly as the paragraph at
59: ## systems_architecture.md:745 says.
60: ##
61: ## ALLOCATE BEFORE CONSUME (decision 0059). Every function here is static and pure over its
62: ## arguments. A refused header or section table has touched no store, no column and no world; the
63: ## caller gets a `Refusal` and decides. Nothing returns a sentinel offset or a zeroed header that
64: ## could be mistaken for a parsed one.

193: # --- CRC-32/ISO-HDLC --------------------------------------------------------------------------
194: 
195: static var _crc_table: PackedInt64Array = PackedInt64Array()
196: 
197: 
198: static func _crc_lookup() -> PackedInt64Array:
199: 	"""Build the 256-entry reflected CRC table once, from the stated reversed polynomial."""
200: 	if _crc_table.size() == 256:
201: 		return _crc_table
202: 	var table: PackedInt64Array = PackedInt64Array()
203: 	table.resize(256)
204: 	for index: int in 256:
205: 		var register: int = index
206: 		for _bit: int in 8:
207: 			if (register & 1) != 0:
208: 				register = (register >> 1) ^ CRC32_REVERSED_POLYNOMIAL
209: 			else:
210: 				register >>= 1
211: 		table[index] = register
212: 	_crc_table = table
213: 	return _crc_table

216: static func crc32_update(register: int, bytes: PackedByteArray) -> int:
217: 	"""Fold `bytes` into a running reflected CRC register. Start from CRC32_INITIAL_REGISTER."""
218: 	var table: PackedInt64Array = _crc_lookup()
219: 	var value: int = register & SaveCodec.UINT32_MAX
220: 	for index: int in bytes.size():
221: 		value = table[(value ^ bytes[index]) & 0xff] ^ (value >> 8)
222: 	return value

225: static func crc32_of(bytes: PackedByteArray) -> int:
226: 	"""CRC-32/ISO-HDLC of exactly these bytes, as an unsigned 32-bit integer."""
227: 	return crc32_update(CRC32_INITIAL_REGISTER, bytes) ^ CRC32_FINAL_XOR

232: static func encode_header_into(header: Header, out: PackedByteArray) -> Refusal:
233: 	"""Write the 256 fixed header bytes into `out` at offset 0, or refuse without writing.
234: 
235: 	Every digest length and every field range is checked BEFORE the first byte is written, so a
236: 	refused encode leaves `out` byte-identical to what the caller handed in.
237: 	"""
238: 	if out.size() < HEADER_BYTES:
239: 		return Refusal.new(REFUSE_HEADER_TRUNCATED,
240: 			"a %d-byte buffer cannot hold the %d-byte header" % [out.size(), HEADER_BYTES])
241: 	var digests: Refusal = digest_lengths_refusal(header)
242: 	if not digests.is_ok():
243: 		return digests
244: 	var ranges: Refusal = _encodable_ranges_refusal(header)
245: 	if not ranges.is_ok():
246: 		return ranges
247: 	var staging: PackedByteArray = PackedByteArray()
248: 	staging.resize(HEADER_BYTES)
249: 	if not _write_header_words(header, staging) or not _write_header_digests(header, staging):
250: 		return Refusal.new(REFUSE_VALUE_RANGE, "a header field could not be encoded")
251: 	var scratch: SaveCodec.Scalar = SaveCodec.Scalar.new()
252: 	if not SaveCodec.write_bytes_into(out, 0, staging, scratch):
253: 		return Refusal.new(REFUSE_HEADER_TRUNCATED, scratch.detail)
254: 	return Refusal.new(REFUSE_NONE, "")

257: static func digest_lengths_refusal(header: Header) -> Refusal:
258: 	"""Every one of the six header digests must be exactly 32 bytes. BLOCKER H2: nothing more."""

276: 			or header.chronicle_record_count < 0 or header.replay_sequence < 0:
277: 		return Refusal.new(REFUSE_VALUE_RANGE, "a u64 header word is negative")

312: static func decode_header_into(bytes: PackedByteArray, out: Header) -> Refusal:
313: 	"""Parse the 256 fixed header bytes into `out`, or refuse without a partial parse.
314: 
315: 	Structural only: it refuses a short buffer and a u64 field a GDScript int cannot hold, and
316: 	does not judge magic, version, tick or file length. `header_refusal()` does that, in
317: 	ARCH-SAVE-004's order.
318: 	"""
319: 	if bytes.size() < HEADER_BYTES:
320: 		return Refusal.new(REFUSE_HEADER_TRUNCATED,
321: 			"a %d-byte buffer is shorter than the %d-byte header" % [bytes.size(), HEADER_BYTES])
322: 	var reader: SaveCodec.Reader = SaveCodec.Reader.new(bytes)
323: 	var parsed: Header = Header.new()
324: 	if not _read_header_words(reader, parsed):
325: 		return Refusal.new(reader.refusal(), reader.detail())
326: 	_read_header_digests(bytes, parsed)
327: 	_copy_header(parsed, out)
328: 	return Refusal.new(REFUSE_NONE, "")

331: static func _read_header_words(reader: SaveCodec.Reader, parsed: Header) -> bool:
332: 	"""Read every integer header word through the bounded reader, in offset order."""
333: 	var scalar: SaveCodec.Scalar = SaveCodec.Scalar.new()
334: 	reader.seek(OFFSET_FORMAT_VERSION)
335: 	parsed.format_version = scalar.value if reader.read_u32_into(scalar) else 0
336: 	parsed.header_bytes = scalar.value if reader.read_u32_into(scalar) else 0
337: 	parsed.endian_sentinel = scalar.value if reader.read_u32_into(scalar) else 0
338: 	parsed.section_count = scalar.value if reader.read_u32_into(scalar) else 0
339: 	parsed.total_file_bytes = scalar.value if reader.read_u64_into(scalar) else 0
340: 	parsed.completed_tick = scalar.value if reader.read_i64_into(scalar) else 0
341: 	reader.seek(OFFSET_SECTION_TABLE_OFFSET)
342: 	parsed.section_table_offset = scalar.value if reader.read_u64_into(scalar) else 0
343: 	parsed.chronicle_record_count = scalar.value if reader.read_u64_into(scalar) else 0
344: 	parsed.replay_sequence = scalar.value if reader.read_u64_into(scalar) else 0
345: 	return not reader.failed()

379: static func magic_refusal(bytes: PackedByteArray) -> Refusal:
380: 	"""ARCH-SAVE-004's first check: the eight ASCII magic bytes, compared byte for byte."""
381: 	if bytes.size() < MAGIC_BYTES:
382: 		return Refusal.new(REFUSE_HEADER_TRUNCATED,
383: 			"a %d-byte buffer cannot hold the magic" % bytes.size())
384: 	if bytes.slice(0, MAGIC_BYTES) != MAGIC.to_ascii_buffer():
385: 		return Refusal.new(REFUSE_MAGIC, "the first %d bytes are not '%s'" % [MAGIC_BYTES, MAGIC])
386: 	return Refusal.new(REFUSE_NONE, "")

389: static func header_refusal(header: Header, available_bytes: int) -> Refusal:
390: 	"""ARCH-SAVE-004's magic/endian/version/tick/length checks over an already parsed header.

390: 	"""ARCH-SAVE-004's magic/endian/version/tick/length checks over an already parsed header.
391: 
392: 	`available_bytes` is the real byte count on disk; ARCH-SAVE-004 requires the "exact file
393: 	length", so a header claiming any other total is refused rather than trusted.
394: 	"""
395: 	var version: Refusal = _version_refusal(header)
396: 	if not version.is_ok():
397: 		return version
